title: Tightness of the MinFS Bound for 4-Bit S-Boxes
summary: An upper bound on MinFS is known for S-boxes without nonzero linear structures, but its tightness and the existence of a 4-bit example with MinFS 3 remain open.

formal_statement.body: For S-boxes without a nonzero linear structure, the established upper bound is $\mathrm{MinFS} \leq \mathrm{DUS}/2 + 1$. No $4$-bit S-box attaining $\mathrm{MinFS}=3$ was found. Determine whether the upper bound is tight, in particular whether a $4$-bit S-box without a nonzero linear structure and with $\mathrm{MinFS}=3$ exists.

scope.domain: Structural analysis of S-boxes and their resistance to differential fault attacks.
assumptions: The S-box has no nonzero linear structure.
parameters: MinFS: the S-box invariant bounded above and targeted at value 3
DUS: the differential-uniformity parameter appearing in the upper bound
S-box width: fixed to 4 bits in the concrete existence question
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the upper bound is tight, particularly whether a 4-bit S-box with no nonzero linear structure and MinFS equal to 3 exists.

citations.label: DEFAULT: Cipher Level Resistance Against Differential Fault Attack

progress.summary: Corollary 1 establishes the upper bound. Remark 2 reports that no 4-bit S-box with MinFS equal to 3 was found and explicitly leaves tightness open for future research.
